title: Khronos OrientationTest -- thirteen drawn primitives over seven materials, which is the draw list and not one subject with one surface

criterion.says: This model tests the orientation supplied by nodes in the hierarchy. ... Thus, if each colored arrow points directly at a target of the same color, the test passes. If an arrow appears to have been rotated away from the target of the same color, it could indicate a misplaced matrix transpose or some other orientation problem.

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (`board/`). Khronos's OrientationTest is a grid of plates at many orientations, which is exactly the case where the slopes cannot agree: E is over a hundred and no single roll serves them.

subjects.name: OrientationTest
subjects.notes: Thirteen mesh-bearing nodes, one primitive each, naming SEVEN materials: a base cube plus six arrow/target pairs, one per signed axis. Six of the nodes carry a TRS and three of those a `matrix`, so the same file also exercises the two spellings of a node transform in one scene. No texture and no uv set: what this case is for is the LIST -- many primitives, each with its own material and its own place in the order -- and a texture would put the sampler back into a comparison that is about the list.

source.pinReason: the same pin every other Khronos subject in this tree carries

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of board:0083 (src/gltf/Framing.h) applied to this subject's own bounds: azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 at r = 9.232958838158792 m, yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL, near = distance - r and far = distance + r. The bounds are min (-5.33065128326416, -5.330651177643153, -5.33065128326416) and max (5.33065128326416, 5.3306513130664825, 5.33065128326416) over the flattened default scene, so the centre is the origin to within one float32 step of the y extent. THE ROLL IS ZERO AND STATED: this subject is a symmetric arrangement about three axes and no roll makes its silhouette rational, so a roll here would be a different draw of the same lottery rather than an exactness argument.
camera.note: THE ENGINE'S OWN ANSWER, QUOTED (board:1398). Every number here is read from the framing rule's output for this subject -- eye, aim, yfov and both clip planes -- rather than recomputed by the authoring helper, which bounded each primitive by the eight transformed corners of its local AABB and therefore always at least as loosely as the engine bounds the transformed vertices. A looser radius moves the eye back, and 93 cases declared a camera the rule does not derive. `ADerivedCameraIsTheFramingRuleAndNotAQuotation` recomputes all of it and refuses a mismatch, so what this declaration does is PIN the viewpoint, never choose it.

light.note: The only illumination is Blender's factory world, and an emitter does not gather it. It is left where it is because configuring it would be a second thing to keep honest.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: ONE COLOUR PER MATERIAL, which is the key a multi-material asset has: a per-NODE colour cannot reach two primitives of one node that name different materials, and that is what SciFiHelmet and AlphaBlendModeTest are. Each colour is the file's own baseColorFactor for that material, verbatim, so the number is recomputable from the pinned asset and the picture is the arrangement the asset was authored to show. Emission and not a Diffuse BSDF because this subject occludes itself -- the arrows stand in front of the cube -- and there Cycles at one sample is a Bernoulli draw on the visible sky fraction, which is an ambient-occlusion estimator wearing a placement's clothes (board:0087). A ShaderNodeEmission at strength 1 gathers nothing, so the world as a light, the sun's disk, a light's radius and visibility all leave at once, and the boundary between two declared colours is exact.

default.note: One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe at another seed, and the whole of the emission case's acceptance. A Monte-Carlo estimator's answer depends on its seed; an emitter has no estimator, so the two dumps must agree bit for bit and any difference NAMES the integral that survived.

notes: Khronos states this asset shows whether an engine's axes and its node transforms agree. Ours adds the question it was blocked on: thirteen primitives over seven materials cannot be drawn by a unit that draws one subject with one surface, so this is the first case whose verdict needs a draw list at all.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's 524 triangles of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the fetched vertices
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so. Every triangle is counted by the magnitude of its signed area, so a closed body counts its far side too and this is an AREA, not a coverage.
